reason: Hypothesis A proposes a physically sound, testable mechanism—gradient nanocrystalline subsurface promoting a protective oxide glaze—that directly addresses high-temperature wear via tribo-oxidation, a known phenomenon in this regime, and extends prior findings on glaze layers, whereas Hypothesis B relies on Cu precipitation strengthening, which is less specific to the high-temperature sliding wear context and may be undermined by precipitate coarsening or dissolution at the intended 600–800 °C operating conditions.
